name: vscode-mcp
description: Exposes VS Code's own commands, tabs, text and extensions to an agent over MCP, like sublime-mcp does for Sublime Text.

vscodeMcp.bind.description: Address the MCP server listens on. Leave on 127.0.0.1 except inside a disposable sandbox, where 0.0.0.0 lets the host reach it. Restart the server after changing it.

vscodeMcp.port.description: First port the MCP server tries (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp). With vscodeMcp.portFallback on, a window whose port is already taken moves to the next free one, so several windows can run this server at once. Restart the server after changing it.

vscodeMcp.extensionsDir.description: Extensions folder this VS Code was started with (--extensions-dir). install_extension and uninstall_extension pass it to VS Code's CLI; empty means the CLI's own default, which is wrong when VS Code runs with a different folder.

vscodeMcp.userDataDir.description: User data folder this VS Code was started with (--user-data-dir), passed to VS Code's CLI the same way. Empty means the CLI's default.

vscodeMcp.exposeAllTools.description: Present every tool in tools/list instead of the core surface plus discover. Off by default: the full list is thousands of tool schemas (one per VS Code command id) and fills a limited-context client before the first message, leaving no room to compact. A client that refuses a tool it was not told about does not need this - batch is always listed and runs any tool by name.

vscodeMcp.portFallback.description: When the configured port is already bound by another window, take the next free port instead of failing (9561, 9562, ...). Off keeps the port pinned, which is what a client that mounts one fixed port wants.
